newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans decree to free export of sugar.
newsitem.headline: India plans decree to free export of sugar.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday proposed a presidential decree to free the export of sugar, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
PTI quoted Deve Gowda as promising the special move to circumvent parliament, where a vote on his proposal to deregulate the export of sugar was deferred on Friday.
The bill seeks to end the monopoly of a private trading agency over sugar exports. The upper house put off the vote saying the bill demanded closer study.
The prime minister was quoted as telling a public meeting in the eastern state of Bihar that a presidential ordinance would facilitate the export of 3.5 million tonnes of sugar stocks.
He said easier exports would "free sugarcane farmers from exploitation."
"In accordance with our policy, we have decided to soon promulgate an ordinance for the purpose so as to clear the arrears of the sugarcane growers in various states in the country," Deve Gowda said.
The bill was earlier approved by the lower house, but needs upper house approval as well before being submitted to the president.
A presidential ordinance can only be issued when parliament is not in session. Parliament closed its winter session on Friday and is scheduled to reconvene in February.

Indian sugar exports are currently channelled through the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corp (ISGIEC), an agency set up by private millers. It is the only body permitted to export sugar.
The bill would permit private firms registered with the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA) to export sugar.
